# Pyramid

2020 ICPC Asia Taipei-Hsinchu Regional
Problem C
Pyramid
Time limit: 3 seconds
Memory limit: 1024 megabytes
Problem Description
Consider an 𝑛×𝑛 grid where nodes are labelled as (𝑖, 𝑗) for 0 ≤ 𝑖, 𝑗 < 𝑛. We rotate it 45 degree
in clockwise direction and keep only its top half part. Then you get a pyramid, as shown in
Figure 1. All of the nodes laid on the anti-diagonal of the grid have labels (𝑛 − 1 − 𝑗, 𝑗) for
0 ≤ 𝑗 < 𝑛. They are located at the bottom line of the pyramid. For simplicity and clarity,
we name node (𝑛 − 1 − 𝑗, 𝑗) as exit 𝑗. Node (0, 0) is called the starting point (labelled as 𝑃
in Figure 1). When you insert a ball from the starting point, this ball will roll down to some
of the exits. A ball located at node (𝑖, 𝑗) can only roll down to either node (𝑖 + 1, 𝑗) or node
(𝑖, 𝑗 + 1), and the ball shall never be broken or split. There is a tiny switch equipped on every
node other than the exits that controls the move direction of the ball, and this switch always
works well. The switch has exactly two states: either 𝐿 or 𝑅, indicates that the ball can move
to node (𝑖 + 1, 𝑗) or (𝑖, 𝑗 + 1), respectively. After the ball leaves this node, the switch changes
immediately to the other state. The default setting for a switch is at 𝐿.
Figure 1: An example for 𝑛 = 5.
When you insert the first ball into 𝑃, this ball will reach exit 0, and the states of nodes (𝑖, 0)
for 0 ≤ 𝑖 < 𝑛 − 1 are now all 𝑅’s. Then you insert the second, third, and so on so forth, one by
one, until the 𝑘
𝑡ℎ ball finishes. The status of every switch accumulates with these balls. Please
write a program to determine the number of the exit point for the 𝑘
𝑡ℎ ball.
Input Format
The first line of the input is a number that specifies the number of test cases. Each test case
has only one line that gives you two space-delimited numbers 𝑛 and 𝑘.
Output Format
Please output the exit number of the 𝑘
𝑡ℎ ball in one line.
5

2020 ICPC Asia Taipei-Hsinchu Regional
Technical Specification
• There are at most 20 test cases.
• 1 ≤ 𝑛 ≤ 104
.
• 1 ≤ 𝑘 ≤ 108
.
Sample Input 1
2
5 1
5 2
Sample Output 1
0
1
Sample Input 2
3
5 3
5 4
5 5
Sample Output 2
2
3
2
6

[PDF](https://icpcarchive.github.io/Asia%20Pacific%20Contests/Taiwan/2020%20Asia%20Taipei-Hsinchu%20Regional%20Contest/problems.pdf)

# Pyramid

Time limit: 3 seconds. Memory limit: 1024 megabytes.

## Problem Description

Consider an $n\times n$ grid whose nodes are labelled $(i,j)$ for $0\le i,j<n$. Rotate it $45^\circ$ clockwise and keep only its top half. This gives a pyramid, as shown in Figure 1. The nodes on the anti-diagonal have labels $(n-1-j,j)$ for $0\le j<n$ and lie on the bottom line of the pyramid. For simplicity, call node $(n-1-j,j)$ exit $j$. Node $(0,0)$ is the starting point, labelled $P$ in Figure 1.

When a ball is inserted at the starting point, it rolls down to an exit. From node $(i,j)$, it can move only to $(i+1,j)$ or $(i,j+1)$; it never breaks or splits. Every node other than an exit has a working switch with exactly two states, $L$ and $R$. These states send the ball to $(i+1,j)$ and $(i,j+1)$, respectively. Immediately after the ball leaves, the switch changes to the other state. Every switch is initially in state $L$.

![Figure 1](102835-C-figure-1.png)

Figure 1: An example with $n=5$.

The first ball inserted at $P$ reaches exit 0, leaving every switch at $(i,0)$ for $0\le i<n-1$ in state $R$. Insert the second, third, and subsequent balls one at a time until the $k$-th ball finishes. Switch states persist between balls. Determine the exit number reached by the $k$-th ball.

## Input Format

The first line contains the number of test cases. Each test case consists of one line with two space-separated numbers $n$ and $k$.

## Output Format

For each test case, output the exit number of the $k$-th ball on one line.

## Technical Specification

- There are at most 20 test cases.
- $1\le n\le10^4$.
- $1\le k\le10^8$.

## Sample 1

### Input

```text
2
5 1
5 2
```

### Output

```text
0
1
```

## Sample 2

### Input

```text
3
5 3
5 4
5 5
```

### Output

```text
2
3
2
```

# 金字塔

时间限制：3 秒。内存限制：1024 兆字节。

## 题目描述

有一个 $n\times n$ 的网格，节点编号为 $(i,j)$，其中 $0\le i,j<n$。将它顺时针旋转 $45^\circ$，只保留上半部分，就得到图 1 所示的金字塔。原网格反对角线上的节点编号为 $(n-1-j,j)$，其中 $0\le j<n$；这些节点位于金字塔的底边上。为方便描述，将节点 $(n-1-j,j)$ 称为出口 $j$。节点 $(0,0)$ 是起点，在图 1 中标为 $P$。

从起点放入一个球后，它会向下滚到某个出口。位于节点 $(i,j)$ 的球只能滚向 $(i+1,j)$ 或 $(i,j+1)$，球不会破裂或分裂。除出口外，每个节点都有一个正常工作的开关。开关只有 $L$ 和 $R$ 两种状态，分别使球滚向 $(i+1,j)$ 和 $(i,j+1)$。球离开节点后，开关立刻切换到另一种状态。所有开关最初均为 $L$ 状态。

![Figure 1](102835-C-figure-1.png)

图 1：$n=5$ 时的例子。

从 $P$ 放入的第一个球会到达出口 0，此时所有满足 $0\le i<n-1$ 的节点 $(i,0)$ 上的开关都变为 $R$。随后依次放入第二个、第三个球，直到第 $k$ 个球滚出。每个开关的状态会保留下来，供后续的球使用。请确定第 $k$ 个球到达的出口编号。

## 输入格式

第一行给出测试用例数。每个测试用例只有一行，包含两个以空格分隔的数 $n$ 和 $k$。

## 输出格式

对于每个测试用例，输出一行，表示第 $k$ 个球到达的出口编号。

## 数据范围

- 测试用例不超过 20 组。
- $1\le n\le10^4$。
- $1\le k\le10^8$。

## 样例 1

### 输入

```text
2
5 1
5 2
```

### 输出

```text
0
1
```

## 样例 2

### 输入

```text
3
5 3
5 4
5 5
```

### 输出

```text
2
3
2
```
